seo.title: Floatboat Agent Workspace — One Place for Agents, Files, and Work
seo.description: Run agents alongside local files, tools, project rules, and editable deliverables in one persistent, human-controlled workspace for Mac and Windows.

hero.title: Give agents a workspace, not another chat window.
hero.description: Floatboat brings agents, local files, models, tools, project rules, and deliverables into one persistent desktop environment—so work can continue from context instead of restarting with every prompt.

demo.title: Keep the project, rules, and results together
demo.description: Agents can work from the same approved files and tools, leave inspectable outputs, and continue from what the project has already learned.

features.title: The environment around the agent is part of the product.
features.description: Floatboat gives work a durable home where context, execution, review, and delivery remain connected.

comparison.title: An Agent Workspace changes what happens after the answer.
comparison.description: The difference is not a larger chat window. It is a persistent environment for doing, reviewing, and continuing real work.

items.question: What is an AI Agent Workspace?
items.answer: It is a persistent work environment where agents can use approved files, tools, models, rules, and prior outputs to complete and continue real projects—not just answer isolated prompts.

items.question: How is this different from the Floatboat Coworker?
items.answer: The Agent Workspace is the environment that holds context and resources over time. The Coworker is a Work Agent you can give a bounded task to and receive a deliverable from.

items.question: Does local-first mean nothing ever leaves my computer?
items.answer: No. Local-first means work begins from your real desktop environment and files. Data handling still depends on the cloud models and connectors you choose, so each external path should be evaluated separately.

items.question: Can more than one agent work in the same workspace?
items.answer: Yes. Floatboat supports multiple agents working from shared project context, with human review, redirection, and approval remaining part of the process.
